To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degradation of polymer films for the high-ohmic resistance protection in a heat/humid environment is determined by three main factors: temperature, hydrogen evolution reaction ( HER ) and corrosion reaction of hydroxide (OH − ) ions.

the degradation behavior and mechanism of the polymer films for high ohmic resistor protection in heat and humid environment are investigated, and the degradation of polymer films mainly formed from phenolic and epoxy resin are mainly caused by corrosion of OH − ions generated by the hydrogen evolution reaction.
the degradation of polymer films in high-ohmic coated resistors in a heat and high humidity environment is mainly caused by the corrosion reaction of OH ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the degradation behavior and mechanism of the polymer films for highohmic resistor protection working in a heat-humid environment.
the mechanism of the polymer film degradation and the influence of temperature, humidity and HER on the degradation of polymer films.
the degradation behavior and mechanism of the polymer films for high resistance protection in a heat-humid environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polymer films are not suitable for high-ohm resistors working in the heat and humid environment.
polymer degradation in high-ohmic coated resistors working in heat and humid environment may be caused by temperature, HER, and corrosion reaction of the OH − ions.

the degradation of polymer films for resistor protection is mainly due to the combined effects of temperature, HER and corrosion resulted from OH ions, which can provide a new perspective for further research on the degradation mechanism of polymer films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the protection of polymer films for the high-ohmic resistance is mainly dependent on the resistance to the corrosion of OH − ions, which is determined by the chemical structure of polymer films and the concentration of OH − ions.

the degradation behavior and mechanism of high-ohm resistor protection polymer films in a heat and humidity environment are mainly dominated by three factors: the temperature, hydrogen evolution reaction and corrosion reaction of hydroxide ions, among which the latter two are found to be the major reasons of the degradation.

temperature is the main driving force of the failure of coated resistor, and the degradation mechanism of polymer films is determined by the competition of the temperature effects and the corrosion effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polymer film for high-ohm resistors should be as thin as possible and the film surface should be as smooth as possible to avoid water penetration.
, for a coated resistor, the polymer degradation is a complicated process and the degradation mechanism is determined by the interaction of various factors.

, for high-ohm resistors working in heat and humid environment at high temperature, the polymer films should be modified with a corrosion inhibitor to prevent corrosion of the metal substrate, and a hydrophobic agent should be used to prevent water penetration into the polymer films.
